TIME TO DEVELOP A DIGITAL TWIN FOR THE HPC 
DATA CENTER 
Luigi Telesca3, Davide De Chiara2, Marco Antonini3, Giovanni Ponti5 and Marta Chinnici1 
1TERIN-ICT Division, HPC Lab, ENEA, R.C. Casaccia, Italy 
2TERIN-ICT Division, HPC Lab, ENEA, R.C. Portici, Italy 
3Trakti Ltd., United Kingdom 
5TERIN-ICT Division, ENEA, Sede, Italy 
ABSTRACT 
High-performance computing (HPC) data centers are facing increasing energy consumption, even though there is a pressing 
need for greater efficiency. By 2030, these facilities are projected to account for 13% of global energy demand, and this 
could rise to as much as 21%. Furthermore, HPC data centers are expected to contribute 8% of global carbon emissions, 
which can result in substantial operational costs, threats to power security, and environmental challenges. Traditional 
methods such as heuristics, statistics, and engineering approaches have proven ineffective in enhancing energy efficiency 
due to the vast number of configurations, complex non-linear parameter interactions, and the enormous volume of 
operational data involved. Therefore, optimizing data centers—particularly HPC clusters—has become a critical issue. The 
integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), sensors, and intelligent devices has significantly increased the generation of 
operational management data from various aspects of the data center industry. By effectively modeling and processing this 
data, it is possible to improve energy efficiency, ensure reliability, reduce operating costs, and sustainably manage data 
centers. The authors propose a holistic approach that utilizes a Blockchain Digital Twin framework, enhanced by Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) processed data, to represent the physical complexities of data centers in virtual and tokenized models. The 
goal of this approach is to achieve real-time prediction, optimization, monitoring, control, and improved decision-making. 
Specifically, the methodology, architecture, and steps taken to develop a scalable analytical dashboard using Blockchain 
technology are detailed. This pioneering Blockchain Digital Twin approach has been tested in a real-world setting, 
specifically at the ENEA HPC Cluster known as CRESCO7. This system learns from actual operational data and enables 
real-time management, monitoring, and control, allowing for comprehensive visibility into the status of the data center and 
optimizing its functionalities. The authors also aim to demonstrate the benefits of the Blockchain Digital Twin approach 
for various stakeholders involved in the data center ecosystem. 
KEYWORDS 
Digital Twin, Data Center, HPC, Energy Efficiency, Data Science, AI 
1. INTRODUCTION 
Data Centers (DCs) are essential for meeting the growing demand for reliable and scalable data processing, 
storage, and networking capabilities that support both businesses and individual users. With the rapid rise in 
demand for digital services and applications, DCs have become widespread, reinforcing the ongoing trend of 
digitization. However, they also present significant challenges in terms of energy costs and carbon emissions 
(Vafamehr et al., 2018). Currently, it is estimated that DCs account for approximately 3% of global energy 
consumption. According to (Andrae et al., 2015) and updates from 2019 (Andrae, 2019), if no action is taken, 
DCs are projected to consume 21% of the global energy demand by 2030. In terms of environmental impact, 
DCs are estimated to contribute 0.3% of global carbon emissions annually (Jones et al., 2018) and are expected 
to rise to 8% by 2030 (Cao et al., 2022). Optimizing the energy efficiency of DCs, particularly  
High-Performance Computing (HPC) clusters, is a pressing concern. The demand for computing resources and 
energy for HPC is steadily increasing, while the energy market transitions to renewable sources and faces 
significant price hikes (Kostenko et al., 2020; Gartner, 2019; Uddin et al., 2015; Shuja et al., 2016; Liu et al., 
2014). This paper introduces a Blockchain Digital Twin framework designed to analyze and reduce energy 
consumption and optimize computing resources in a real-world HPC system. The Digital Twin approach

utilizes the innovative HPC cluster at the Italian National Agency for New Technologies, Energy and 
Sustainable Economic Development (ENEA), known as the CRESCO7 cluster in R.C. Portici, Italy. The 
Digital Twin framework gathers information from multiple internal and external data sources to explore various 
optimization opportunities, represent physical assets and intangible resources using Blockchain technology, 
and tokenize infrastructure to promote more accountable and sustainable consumption of HPC resources. It 
also incorporates a scheduling simulation framework that uses data from the Digital Twin and real-world job 
traces to examine the impact of different parameters on the HPC cluster (Chinnici et al., 2023; Grishina et al., 
2022; Grishina et al., 2020; De Chiara et al., 2020). To facilitate operation and energy management based on a 
data-driven, AI-based framework that models DC efficiency, the authors developed an Analytical Dashboard. 
This dashboard enables the management, monitoring, and near real-time visualization of data related to the 
actual DC utilizing Blockchain technology.  For implementing the analytical dashboard, hardware and software 
resources have been modeled as a Digital Twin. Blockchain and tokenization technologies will be used to 
allocate computing resources (HPC loads) efficiently, thus optimizing energy consumption across various 
activities. Our approach, which is rigorously trained and tested using real operational data from the  
ENEA-HPC DC CRESCO7 cluster, leverages the unique capabilities of the Digital Twin approach. This 
innovative method not only provides a physical representation of the DC system but also dynamically adjusts 
parameters through programming, generating numerous samples to aid in model training and enhance fault 
tolerance. According to Gartner, the rise of Digital Twins in industries, particularly when combined with AI 
technology, will facilitate open, connected, and coordinated intelligent environments. The seamless integration 
and real-time exchange of data between the physical and Digital Twin systems allow for real-time energy 
consumption simulations and energy-saving controls. Thus, the combination of AI and Blockchain 
technologies in building the Digital Twin fosters research into adaptive, intelligent, and fault-tolerant energy 
savings schemes for DCs in a flexible and dynamic manner. To develop green and safe DCs, this paper proposes 
a novel energy-saving solution. With its real-time management, monitoring, and control capabilities, the Digital 
Twin DC approach offers a comprehensive visualization of the entire DC, enhancing its status coverage and 
functionality optimization. We also aim to showcase the potential benefits of the Digital Twin DC challenge 
to stakeholders. By utilizing Blockchain to tokenize High-Performance Computing (HPC) assets and 
implement Smart Contracts, we have significantly improved transparency, evidenced by a 40% increase in cost 
visibility for shared resources. This technology enables real-time resource accounting and robust process 
control, aligning HPC operations with stringent Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) criteria, which 
are crucial for organizations striving to meet rigorous ESG standards. 
The remainder of this paper is organized as follows: Section 1 introduce the paper ‘topic; Section 2 
describes the methodology and architecture for building the Digital Twin Data Center using a holistic approach 
and presents the results; Section 3 concludes the paper.  
1.1 Digital Twin: A Facilitator for a Comprehensive Approach 
Data centers, due to their complex nature, serve a dual purpose in the implementation of Digital Twins: 
1. They support the creation and management of Digital Twins (DT). 
2. They act as a Digital Twin themselves, providing a virtual representation of the entire process to manage 
data consumption and optimize processing. 
A Digital Twin can be defined as a virtual representation of a physical asset, enabled by data and simulators, 
for real-time prediction, optimization, monitoring, control, and improved decision-making. The holistic 
approach is grounded in the baseline of Data Center High-Performance Computing (HPC). 
This approach consists of three main pillars: 
1. Virtual Twin: This involves creating a virtual representation of a physical asset or device. Mathematical 
models and computer science techniques are utilized to facilitate this creation. 
2. Predictive Twin: This component utilizes physics-based, data-driven, or hybrid models that operate on 
the virtual twin to predict the behavior of the physical asset. AI and machine learning techniques are employed 
to analyze the data coming into the physical model. 
3. Twin Projection: This step integrates insights generated by the predictive twin into operations and 
processes. The value additions of the Digital Twin include predictive maintenance, operational strategies, 
optimization strategies, energy efficiency, remote monitoring and control, enhanced safety, risk assessment, 
and more efficient, informed decision support systems.

The proposed Digital Twin serves as an enabler for a holistic approach to improving energy efficiency and 
addressing sustainability issues in HPC data centers through the use of blockchain technology. To tackle the 
overfitting problem caused by insufficient samples, the authors implemented a comprehensive approach based 
on asset tokenization, an analytical blockchain solution, and AI. The experimental phase was conducted on the 
ENEA-HPC Cluster, known as CRESCO 7, which has a capacity of 1.4 PetaFLOPS. 
2. METHODOLOGY 
The methodology adopted in this work for creating an advanced Digital Twin model involved leveraging AI 
to enhance and refine raw data from the ENEA High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems (CRESCO7) for 
integration into a Blockchain framework. This process culminated in a tokenized representation of HPC 
resources. The approach is holistic and multifaceted, broken down into several key phases: 
1. Data Collection and Preprocessing 
2. AI-Driven Data Augmentation 
3. Tokenization of HPC Resources 
4. Validation and Testing 
5. Ethical and Regulatory Compliance 
Our methodology enhances the utility of HPC data and facilitates a more granular and dynamic 
representation of HPC resources (see Fig. 1). This has the potential to revolutionize the management and 
utilization of powerful computing platforms, offering stakeholders a glimpse into the future of HPC resource 
management. Thanks to our work on data augmentation, we obtained advanced data to initiate the design of 
the Digital Twin. To further improve the management and allocation of HPC computing resources, we decided 
to digitize hardware and software resources using Blockchain technology. This allowed for the secure 
representation and creation of the Digital Twin, leveraging augmented data provided by AI components. Due 
to its decentralized, transparent, and immutable nature, Blockchain is an ideal platform for creating Digital 
Twins. When applied to HPC resources, Blockchain provides a robust and secure method to represent the 
physical state and behavior of the HPC, while adding usage rules via Smart Contracts. This allows for 
comprehensive and efficient monitoring and management of computational assets. The use of a distributed 
Blockchain infrastructure and tokenization techniques is not just theoretical; we are actively using these tools 
to tokenize and account for computing resources (HPC loads) in a manner that optimizes infrastructure energy 
consumption for various activities (HPC jobs) initiated by users. Our innovative approach involves tokenizing 
resources and allocating them based on workload and request patterns. This ensures efficient and transparent 
resource management that aligns with the dynamic demands of modern data center operations. It is a unique 
solution set to revolutionize the management of HPC computing resources. In this context, to accurately 
represent the Digital Twin of the HPC, three main Blockchain concepts had to be embedded: Identity, 
Tokenization, and Certification. First, each physical asset, such as an HPC scheduler or node, was assigned a 
unique Digital Identity. This identity is made immutable and tamper-proof thanks to the inherent properties of 
Blockchain, facilitating precise tracking and management of each asset while ensuring high accountability and 
traceability. Secondly, through Tokenization, we converted physical assets into digital tokens that represent 
ownership or usage rights. This meant creating tokens for computational power, storage capacity, and energy 
consumption for HPC resources. Each token can be traded, tracked, and managed on the Blockchain, 
transforming otherwise intangible HPC resources into tangible digital assets. Tokenization not only enables 
efficient resource allocation but also provides a high degree of flexibility, allowing for management and control 
of resource usage according to needs. This approach facilitates a real-time, rule-based, smart-contract-centric 
accounting methodology that abstracts away the complexities of standard accounting methods, benefiting from 
the transparency that Blockchain offers [Telesca, L. et al., 2020]. Through smart contracts, we defined the 
algorithm and model used to calculate the energy consumption of each job launched on the HPC. This 
consumption is converted into the corresponding token amount, which is automatically charged to the user 
upon job completion. This entire operation occurs automatically at the end of job execution, and the results are 
permanently stored on the Blockchain, easily verifiable by all, complete with clear parameters outlining how 
the calculations were performed. For the model used to calculate consumption for each job, a custom algorithm 
was developed specifically for this use case. This is not a simple static mathematical formula; instead, it 
accounts for the environment in which it is implemented, reflecting the HPC’s status during runtime.

The algorithm was finely tuned to promote and incentivize users to utilize the available resources more 
efficiently and thoughtfully through a combination of incentives and penalties, which depend on the behavior 
of the job — and thus, by extension, the behavior of the user who launched it. Practically, this translates into a 
calculation model that, given the continual nature of HPC nodes, aims to redistribute a portion of the upkeep 
cost (energy consumed by the nodes, cooling systems, switches, and storage stack) back to the users based on 
their resource usage. The job's behavior is also considered in calculating the final amount the user must pay, 
with a particular focus on how resources are utilized. For instance, part of the algorithm calculates the 
efficiency of CPU utilization for a job and assigns a penalty if it is deemed too low, as this is considered a 
waste of resources. The ultimate goal of this algorithm is to create an independent and autonomous  
high-performance computing (HPC) environment from an economic perspective, while also educating users 
on how to utilize resources more efficiently and thoughtfully. Additionally, "Certification" refers to the issuing 
of digital certificates that verify the compliance and authenticity of an asset, a computation byproduct, or, in 
this case, a reward for specific behaviors. In particular, certificates are minted as rewards for the HPC in 
response to executing what we define as "net-positive jobs." Net-positive jobs are those that fully utilize all the 
resources they request (e.g., high CPU and memory efficiency) and contribute positively to an environmental 
or social cause. For example, a job that supports medical research may fall into this category. These certificates 
store and attest to the total amount of CO2 emitted by the HPC during the execution of these jobs, thereby 
reflecting the jobs' energy efficiency, operational performance, adherence to Environmental, Social, and 
Governance (ESG) criteria, and compliance with regulatory standards. Once the certificates are minted, the 
aim is to establish a global market motivated by companies' need to improve their ESG scores. The principle 
is straightforward: a company seeking to reduce its CO2 emissions can purchase the certificates generated by 
the HPC for executing specific jobs, effectively offloading those emissions and lowering their total CO2 output. 
At the same time, this process contributes directly to the upkeep and maintenance of the HPC.

2.1 HPC Digital Twin Visualization 
The Digital Twin is seamlessly integrated with an advanced dashboard system that visualizes data, creating an 
immersive and interactive environment for monitoring and managing the data center (DC) cluster. Modern 
DCs utilize these integrated dashboard systems to provide a comprehensive view of the collected data. These 
dashboards offer a holistic overview of the DCs' operations, including performance metrics, energy 
consumption, and user activity. Digital Twin of both hardware and software resources, facilitating tokenization 
and efficient resource allocation based on real-time demands. This integration enhances operational efficiency 
while ensuring transparency and security in resource management. The Digital Twin of the ENEA  
High-Performance Computing (HPC) system allows for complete simulation and real-time monitoring of 
computational processes, energy consumption, and cost estimations. By integrating blockchain technology and 
smart contracts, this framework establishes a secure, transparent, and automated management system for HPC 
resources. By offering these two levels of representation, we ensure comprehensive management of HPC 
resources, from overall system operations to detailed node-level monitoring. This dual approach optimizes 
resource usage, improves energy efficiency, and guarantees compliance with best practices.

3. CONCLUSION 
In this work, the authors aim to create a comprehensive, self-sustaining system that optimizes the performance 
of the ENEA HPC CRESCO 7 cluster and sets a benchmark for sustainable data center (DC) operations 
worldwide. We would like to conclude our work by summarizing our most important contributions, particularly 
in relation to blockchain technology. By utilizing blockchain to tokenize high-performance computing (HPC) 
assets and implementing efficiency-based smart contracts, we have achieved several significant benefits. 
Firstly, there has been a 40% increase in the visibility of costs associated with using shared resources, which 
enhances transparency. This improvement allows users to better understand and manage their resource 
consumption.  Our approach is scalable and replicable in other HPC contexts. In the future, we plan to refine 
our models further and integrate additional data sources to improve the accuracy and functionality of the AI 
engine, enhancing the detail of the Digital Twin.

Abstract: High-performance computing (HPC) data centers are facing increasing energy consumption, even though there is a pressing need for greater efficiency. By 2030, these facilities are projected to account for 13% of global energy demand, and this could rise to as much as 21%. Furthermore, HPC data centers are expected to contribute 8% of global carbon emissions, which can result in substantial operational costs, threats to power security, and environmental challenges. Traditional methods such as heuristics, statistics, and engineering approaches have proven ineffective in enhancing energy efficiency due to the vast number of configurations, complex non-linear parameter interactions, and the enormous volume of operational data involved. Therefore, optimizing data centers—particularly HPC clusters—has become a critical issue. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), sensors, and intelligent devices has significantly increased the generation of operational management data from various aspects of the data center industry. By effectively modeling and processing this data, it is possible to improve energy efficiency, ensure reliability, reduce operating costs, and sustainably manage data centers. The authors propose a holistic approach that utilizes a Blockchain Digital Twin framework, enhanced by Artificial Intelligence (AI) processed data, to represent the physical complexities of data centers in virtual and tokenized models. The goal of this approach is to achieve real-time prediction, optimization, monitoring, control, and improved decision-making. Specifically, the methodology, architecture, and steps taken to develop a scalable analytical dashboard using Blockchain technology are detailed. This pioneering Blockchain Digital Twin approach has been tested in a real-world setting, specifically at the ENEA HPC Cluster known as CRESCO7. This system learns from actual operational data and enables real-time management, monitoring, and control, allowing for comprehensive visibility into the status of the data center and optimizing its functionalities. The authors also aim to demonstrate the benefits of the Blockchain Digital Twin approach for various stakeholders involved in the data center ecosystem.
